subject: Re: Renewal and capacity uplift — tranche-based credit proposal
messages:
From: Aisha Mirza <aisha@maplegrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + capacity request (Q1)

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the December discussions. We're approaching our renewal window and two things are top of mind for procurement: a) we need to secure an additional 120k GPU-minutes/month starting Feb, and b) we need more predictable pricing while our usage spikes during the product launch.

Attached is our Q4 usage export for context. Our procurement team has told me they need a formal pricing position and an estimated invoice schedule to route a PO by Jan 28.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a temporary price hold for the term renewal and a tranche credit structure tied to the commit increase? If you have standard language or a term sheet I can share with our buyer that helps map the PO to invoices, that would speed things up.

I can be flexible on contract length (12–24 months) but the provisioning timeline is tight — ideally capacity staged in Feb.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Mirza
Head of Infrastructure
MapleGrid, Inc.

Attachments: MapleGrid_Usage_Q4_2026.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Mirza <aisha@maplegrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity request (Q1)

Hi Aisha — really appreciate the usage file, that helps.

Short answer: yes — we can structure a tranche credit tied to the uplift and offer a short-term price hold for the renewal period to give you invoice predictability while you go live. Two quick notes before I send a formal term sheet:
- I need to align with Finance (looping in David) on exact credit percentages and the invoice cadence.
- I want to confirm the provisioning lead time for your requested 120k GPU-minutes/month so Engineering can reserve the pool.

I attached a draft term sheet (Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf) that outlines a tranche credit approach and a conditional price-hold window — it's a starting point. Can you confirm: is the procurement PO tied to a single invoice or multiple invoices over the term? That affects how we map credits on the invoice schedule.

If it's helpful, I'm available for a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the sheet with procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success & Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity request (Q1)

Marissa — adding a quick internal note before we circulate the redline:

I think a tranche model tied to committed uplift is the right pattern here. My suggested starting structure (internal only):
- Tranche A: +120k GPU-minutes/month for the first 3 months; 8% one-time credit applied against the first invoice after go-live if MapleGrid signs a 12-month commit for the uplift.
- Tranche B: additional +80k GPU-minutes/month activated month 4; 4% one-time credit applied if aggregate usage for months 4–6 exceeds the forecast.
- Price hold: I don't want to lock a permanent discount — recommend a limited price hold of 60 days post signature, during which we won't increase published rates for the SKUs covered by the commit.

Operational asks: Engineering needs a firm provisioning window (calendar dates) and Procurement needs the invoice/PO mapping. David — can you confirm billing mechanics for the one-time credits (credit memos vs. invoice offset)?

Ben
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Mirza <aisha@maplegrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity request (Q1)

Thanks — both of those options are in the right direction. A few counterpoints from procurement and finance:

- Procurement prefers price certainty for at least the first 6 months after renewal because our customer-facing launch budgets are locked in. A 60-day hold is short for them.
- The team is open to tranche credits but would like the first tranche credit to be 10% (not 8%) and would prefer the credit to be applied as an invoice deduction immediately on the first invoice rather than a later credit memo.
- For provisioning: we need the first tranche capacity live by Feb 1 to support staging and internal test runs; full capacity by Mar 1.

We can do a 12-month commit. The key gating item for us is invoice mapping so our PO ties directly to the invoice schedule. Can you update the draft term sheet with an explicit invoice schedule and confirm whether Redwood can apply the first tranche credit as an immediate invoice deduction instead of a separate credit memo entry?

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this — our procurement lead (cc'ed) is ready to work through a redline.

Best,
Aisha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Mirza <aisha@maplegrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jan 2027 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity request (Q1)

Aisha — thanks for the clarity and the timeline. Final proposal below; I've attached an updated SOW and the redlined term sheet for signature.

What we can offer (compromise):
- Price hold: 90-day price hold from signature across covered SKUs (covers procurement's need for short-term certainty).
- Tranche credits: First tranche credit 8% applied as an invoice deduction on the first invoice after go-live (we can post the deduction on that invoice, not as a later credit memo). Second tranche credit 4% applied as an invoice deduction once the second tranche is activated and usage threshold is met.
- Provisioning: Staged provisioning — initial tranche available week of Feb 8; full requested uplift by Mar 1. We will prioritize your pool for that window if we receive signed agreement by Jan 20.
- Commit: 12-month commit covering the uplift. If you sign a 24-month term we can make the first tranche credit 10% instead of 8% (adds the long-term commitment incentive).

Next steps: I've uploaded the final term sheet to DocuSign (link below) and attached the SOW. If procurement can sign by Jan 20 we'll hold the capacity window and confirm the provisioning timetable.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/companies/67890
Docs: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDeFgHiJkLmNoPqRstUvWxY

David — can you confirm we can record the first tranche as an invoice deduction when billing?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
